description: We are Miva-AlphaOne, a collaborative team participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. We are developing AgriShif AI, a solution that uses NASA Earth observation data to help farmers understand changing environmental conditions, identify agricultural risks and make better-informed decisions. Our team brings together interests in software dev, data analysis, geospatial technology, agriculture and AI. We welcome passionate contributors who want to build practical, impactful solutions.
summary:
What if farmers could test tomorrow's climate before making today's farming decisions?

AgriShift AI is a climate-resilient agricultural decision-support platform that transforms NASA Earth observation data into actionable farming insights. Built around its flagship feature, Climate Twin, the platform allows farmers to simulate changes in rainfall, temperature, and water availability and explore how different conditions could affect crop rotation suitability.

By combining historical NASA POWER climate data with farm-specific conditions, soil information, and crop characteristics, AgriShift AI generates and compares potential crop rotation strategies through an explainable, rule-based decision engine. Farmers can explore alternative scenarios, understand the trade-offs behind recommendations, and access climate insights through an interactive dashboard.

Designed with smallholder farmers and agricultural extension workers in mind, AgriShift AI bridges the gap between complex Earth observation data and practical agricultural planning.

Don't Just Predict the Climate. Prepare for It.
details:
Agriculture is increasingly affected by unpredictable rainfall, changing temperatures, water availability, and other climate-related challenges. For smallholder farmers, these changes can make decisions about what to plant and how to manage their farms increasingly difficult.

AgriShift AI addresses this challenge by translating NASA Earth observation data into practical, understandable agricultural insights. The platform helps farmers explore historical climate conditions, understand environmental patterns, and compare potential crop rotation strategies based on their farm conditions.

At the heart of the platform is Climate Twin, an interactive simulator that allows users to explore hypothetical changes in rainfall, temperature, and water availability and examine how different crop rotation options respond to these scenarios. Rather than simply presenting environmental statistics, AgriShift AI makes climate information interactive and relevant to agricultural planning.

Our intended beneficiaries include smallholder farmers, agricultural extension workers, and agricultural researchers. By making Earth observation data more accessible and understandable, the project supports informed agricultural decisions and contributes to broader efforts towards climate resilience, sustainable food systems, and the practical application of Earth science.

This approach aligns with NASA's vision of making Earth science and observation data useful beyond research institutions, enabling people and communities to better understand and respond to changes in their environment.


AgriShift AI was developed as a full-stack web application using Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui for the frontend, with Python and FastAPI powering the backend. PostgreSQL supports data management, while Pandas and NumPy support data processing. Recharts and Leaflet provide data visualisation and geographical context.

The platform integrates NASA POWER data to retrieve historical climate information, particularly rainfall and temperature parameters. This information is processed and presented through an interactive dashboard.

A major part of our implementation is the explainable, rule-based crop rotation engine. It evaluates potential crop sequences using factors such as climate conditions, soil type, water availability, previous crops, and user priorities. Our Climate Twin extends this functionality by allowing users to modify selected environmental variables and explore how those changes influence the comparison of rotation strategies.

Use of Artificial Intelligence: AI-assisted tools, including ChatGPT and coding assistance tools, supported parts of our development process. Their contributions included brainstorming, technical research, troubleshooting, debugging, coding assistance, and documentation refinement. However, AI was not the central decision-making engine of the application. The project's core functionality is built around our team's own system architecture, NASA data integration, rule-based evaluation logic, interface development, and implementation decisions.

Our team directed the development process, determined the project's functionality, designed the user experience, implemented the application components, and worked on integrating the different systems into a functional product. AI tools served as development aids rather than substitutes for our engineering work or the project's underlying methodology.

AgriShift AI demonstrates how accessible Earth observation data, thoughtful software engineering, and interactive decision-support systems can come together to address a practical agricultural challenge.
